therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Sequential high-dose chemotherapy with autologous rescue followed by non-myeloablative allogeneic transplant for graft-versus-lymphoma effect
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: Eradication of residual lymphoma cells through cytoreduction and allogeneic immune-mediated anti-tumor effect
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Patients with various lymphoma subtypes including DLBCL, low-grade lymphoma, T-cell lymphoma, mantle cell lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and CLL
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Donor chimerism ≥80% at day 100 post-allogeneic transplant

results.target_engagement_evidence: Successful donor engraftment with median 95% donor chimerism at day 100
biomarker_changes: Median neutrophil recovery at 12 days post-allogeneic transplant
subgroup_findings: Participants completing both transplants: 2-year PFS 72% (95% CI: 55-83%), 2-year OS 89% (95% CI: 74-96%)
Participants with autologous transplant only: 2-year PFS 46% (95% CI: 23-66%), 2-year OS 69% (95% CI: 43-85%)
safety_signals: Serious adverse events: respiratory failure, sepsis, ARDS, AV block, death (1 case each)
results.dose_information: Autologous conditioning: Busulfan 0.8 mg/kg Q6H days -8 to -5, Etoposide 30 mg/kg day -4, Cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg days -3,-2. Allogeneic conditioning: Fludarabine 30 mg/m2/day days -5 to -2, Busulfan 0.8 mg/kg/day days -5 to -2
